newsitem.title: MEXICO: Three consortia apply to bid for Mexican railroad.
newsitem.headline: Three consortia apply to bid for Mexican railroad.

text.p: Three consortia applied to bid for Mexico's Pacific-North railroad, the Communication and Transport Ministry's privatization coordinator, Jorge Silberstein, said on Monday.

The applicants were: U.S. Union Pacific Corp. with Mexican builder Empresas ICA Sociedad Controladora SA; Mexican miners Grupo Mexico SA; and Mexican builder Grupo Tribasa SA with Impulsora Tlaxcalteca de Industrias (ITISA) and Railtex Service Co Inc, Silberstein told Reuters.
Bids due on June 19 and a decision is expected by July 7.

The government is auctioning off an 80 percent operating concession for the 6,500-km railway network. It stretches from five cities on the U.S. border, through Manzanillo, Guaymas, Mazatlan and Tampico ports, with connections to the city centers of Monterrey, Guadalajara and Mexico City.
U.S. border connections are at Mexicali, Nogales, Ciudad Juarez, Piedras Negras and Ojinaga.

The winning bidder will have the option to buy the smaller Chihuahua-Pacifico line, which connects Ojinaga on the Rio Grande to the port of Topolobampo. The route will be sold at a price established by the government by May 24, "based on expected cash flow," Silberstein said.
